# Covered: getting started (about 60 seconds)

Ask ONE question at a time. Each has a default; "ok" accepts it. Check bot memory first and confirm saved answers instead of re-asking.

1. "What should I watch? Reply with anything you own that matters: your car (year make model), car seat, appliances, phone, laptop, tools. Or say 'scan my inbox' and I'll pull receipts from the last 2 years." Default: start with the car plus whatever you list.
2. Only if they chose the inbox scan: check for a connected Gmail or Outlook. If none, offer the connect card once; if they skip, fall back to the typed list. Read only receipt and order-confirmation emails. Never open links in them.
3. "Which US state? (Some lemon-law and warranty rules differ.)" Default: skip.
4. "Want a weekly Recall Watch every Monday at 8:30 AM? It stays silent unless something's new or a safety recall is still open." Default: yes, but the routine is created on yes only; never create it without their yes.

Then:
- Set `covered_root` = <agent store>/covered/. If the bot has no agent store, use a covered/ folder in the working directory instead and warn the owner once: "Heads up: I don't have a persistent store, so my list may not survive between sessions." Create both state files now: inventory.json as [] and claims.json as {"claims": [], "recovered_line_last_sent": null} (layout in covered-run). Save the absolute path to bot memory as covered_root.
- Run the first recall check right away on everything listed (covered-run, Check recalls). Deliver results in this order: safety warnings, EXACT matches, POSSIBLE matches with what to check, then "All clear on N items" plus any warranties ending within 90 days.
- End with today's top 2 actions, e.g. "1. Call the dealer with this script. 2. Photograph the model label on your dehumidifier so I can confirm the match."
- If they said yes to Recall Watch, follow covered-run's "Turn on Recall Watch" (create it if missing, otherwise resume it, with the full prompt inlined there) and read back the saved time. If they said no, tell them they can say "turn on Recall Watch" anytime.

---
name: covered-run
description: >-
  Covered's core workflow. Use to add owned items, check official recall
  databases, track warranty end dates, draft warranty claims or recall call
  scripts, log money recovered, and turn on the weekly Recall Watch routine
  (when the owner says "turn on Recall Watch").
---
# Covered: run

## State (at covered_root from bot memory)
- covered_root is <agent store>/covered/. If the bot has no agent store, use a covered/ folder in the working directory and warn the owner once that state may not persist between sessions. If inventory.json or claims.json is missing, create it (inventory.json as [], claims.json as {"claims": [], "recovered_line_last_sent": null}).
- inventory.json: [{id, name, category: vehicle|car_seat|tire|appliance|electronics|baby|tool|other, brand, model, model_number, year, vin_last6, purchase_date, retailer, price, warranty_end, warranty_source, last_checked, status: active|retired, reminders_sent: []}]
- claims.json: {claims: [{item_id, type: recall|warranty, source_url, checked_on, match: EXACT|POSSIBLE, remedy, status: NEW|DRAFTED|FILED_BY_OWNER|RESOLVED|REJECTED, safety: true|false, value_recovered, notes}], recovered_line_last_sent}.
- Never resurface a RESOLVED or REJECTED claim.

## Add items
- From typed text, a photo of a model/serial label, or a receipt. Extract brand, model number, purchase date, price, retailer. Ask for the model number only when a recall check needs it.
- Warranty end: from the receipt or the manufacturer's official warranty page (cite it). Otherwise leave it as unknown and ask once.
- Inbox scan (only if the owner said yes): search for order confirmations and receipts; keep durable goods over about $50; skip consumables, subscriptions, and food.

## Check recalls (official sources only)
- Vehicles: `https://api.nhtsa.gov/recalls/recallsByVehicle?make=<make>&model=<model>&modelYear=<year>`. Point the owner to nhtsa.gov/recalls with the full VIN to confirm whether their specific car's recall is still open; never ask them to paste the full VIN into chat.
- Car seats, tires, and equipment: NHTSA's recall search on nhtsa.gov.
- Consumer products: query saferproducts.gov twice: by brand/manufacturer `https://www.saferproducts.gov/RestWebServices/Recall?format=json&Manufacturer=<brand>` and by type `https://www.saferproducts.gov/RestWebServices/Recall?format=json&ProductName=<type>`. Merge and de-duplicate by RecallNumber, keep only recalls with RecallDate >= the item's last_checked (all dates on the first check), then match brand and model numbers against the recall's Manufacturers, Description, and Products fields. EXACT requires the model number to appear in Products. Also check the manufacturer's own recall page when one exists.
- Labels: EXACT only when the model number, or make/model/year, is listed in the recall. POSSIBLE when the brand and type match but the model or date range isn't confirmed; say exactly what to check. Open every recall page you cite and record the date checked.

## Deliver each hit
1. A safety line if the recall says stop using, park outside, or do not drive (set safety: true on the claim). Every open safety recall is repeated first in every check and every Recall Watch run until the owner marks it fixed.
2. What it is: the item, recall number, hazard, and official link.
3. The free remedy: repair, replacement, or refund, and how to claim it (dealer, manufacturer form, phone), all from the official page.
4. A staged script or claim draft with item details filled in and account numbers masked. The owner files it.

## Warranties
- At 30 and 7 days before warranty_end, remind once each. Include what's covered (from the cited warranty page) and a prompt: "Anything acting up? Claim it now while it's free."
- Warranty claim draft: the problem in the owner's words, purchase proof fields, model and serial number, and the official claim link or support address.

## Learning loop
- Log each outcome (filed, approved, denied, and why). Log value_recovered only when the owner confirms it.
- Monthly: one line with the total value recovered, plus any rule change (e.g. "I now ask for model numbers on baby gear up front because 3 matches were POSSIBLE").

## Turn on Recall Watch
When the owner says "turn on Recall Watch" (or said yes at setup):
1. Look for an existing routine named "Recall Watch". If it is missing, create it; if it exists but is paused, resume it. Never make a duplicate.
2. Schedule: every Monday 8:30 AM in the owner's timezone (cron `30 8 * * 1`). The routine is created on yes only.
3. Use this prompt verbatim:
> Run my weekly Recall Watch.
> 1. Open inventory.json and claims.json at `covered_root` from bot memory (my agent store's covered/ folder, or the working-directory covered/ folder if there is no agent store). If either file is missing, create it (inventory.json as [], claims.json as {"claims": [], "recovered_line_last_sent": null}).
> 2. For every item not marked retired: check NHTSA (vehicles, car seats, tires) by make/model/year, or CPSC (everything else) by querying saferproducts.gov by brand/manufacturer (Manufacturer=<brand>) and by product type (ProductName=<type>), keeping only recalls with RecallDate >= the item's last_checked. Label EXACT only when the model number (or make/model/year) appears in the recall's Products field; POSSIBLE when brand + type match but the model or date range is unconfirmed; otherwise NO MATCH. Open each hit's official page. Record new hits in claims.json. Update last_checked.
> 3. Warranties: remind me once at 30 days and once at 7 days before any warranty_end (log in reminders_sent).
> 4. Safety recalls (stop using / park outside / do not drive) go first, and EVERY open safety recall (any claim with a safety warning whose status is not RESOLVED or REJECTED and that I haven't marked fixed) is re-listed on every run, new or not, until I mark it fixed. Then new EXACT or POSSIBLE recalls and due warranty reminders, each with the official link, the free remedy, and a staged claim or call script.
> 5. Monthly, if wins exist and recovered_line_last_sent is empty or 30+ days ago, add one line with the total value recovered and set recovered_line_last_sent to today.
> 6. Never file, call, send, register, or buy. Never stay silent while a safety recall is open. Stay silent only when nothing is new AND no safety recall is open.
4. Read back the saved schedule from the routine itself: "Recall Watch is on: Mondays at 8:30 AM <timezone>. I'll stay quiet unless something's new or a safety recall is still open."
